orientation_check: The new SCOPE (c) text (l.110-115) and REPORT labels[0].questions[1] are true. They are the corrected statement AUDIT-1 proposed, re-derived here against l.729-731 and l.898-922. (1) Reversing the orientation of HS^2 replaces theta by conj o theta (IsOrientedTangent, vol3), so linkToRP1 becomes c o linkToRP1, with c = conj on RP1 = Circle, since mk(conj z) = conj(mk z). Its lift is c~ x = -x, because proj t = exp(2 pi i t). The developing lift c~ o D decreases, so the canonical orientation flips (l.729-731). The reparametrised D'(s) = -D(-s) increases, and D'(s+1) = c~ f^{-1} c~ D'(s), so f' = c~ f^{-1} c~. Since delta is central and c~ delta^{-k} c~ = delta^k, f' = delta^k (c~ g^{-1} c~): same k. The fixed points of g' are minus those of g, and g' has the same nature as g (it is PGL-conjugate to g^{-1}). Its translation number is tau(f') = -tau(f^{-1}) = tau(f), so the angle is the same. (2) I^+ depends on the time orientation (l.820), not on the orientation of HS^2, and it is read through the new parametrisation, so I'^+ = -I^+. For x in I^+, g'(-x) = -g^{-1}(x) >= -x iff g^{-1} x <= x iff g x >= x. So the sign of l.915 is preserved, and with x ranging over all of RP1~, so is the light-like sign of l.919-921 and the parabolic classes of l.748-749. (3) Reversing RP1~ alone (l.676): gamma_0 -> gamma_0^{-1} and delta -> delta^{-1}, so f^{-1} = (delta^{-1})^k g^{-1}. The degree is unchanged and g' = g^{-1}, with >= reversed, so positivity is preserved again. This is the same mirror read in different coordinates. (4) Lean already agrees in one instance: GX.hasLiftedHolonomy_link holds for every theta, oriented or not, with holonomy delta^2 (l.2173), as (1) predicts for central holonomy. (5) Remark l.926-931 (a conjugacy between g and g^{-1} permutes the components) is consistent: the mirror is not an isomorphism of (Gamma_p, l(p))-circles. It only shows that the invariants do not depend on the convention. 'This is a convention only' and 'So the question is only which convention the author wants recorded' are therefore accurate, and the invariance is correctly marked 'not formalized'.

audit1_resolution.finding: AUDIT-1 major: SCOPE (c) and the REPORT orientation question claimed that the opposite orientation exchanges positive and negative circles
audit1_resolution.how: The clause is gone from both files: grep for 'exchange' or 'positive and negative' finds nothing in RP1Circles.lean or REPORT.json. The replacement text, SCOPE (c) l.110-115 and REPORT labels[0].questions[1], is true: see orientation_check. The question is reduced to the choice of convention.

audit1_resolution.finding: AUDIT-1 minor: the double-cover reading of l.770 was not in SCOPE
audit1_resolution.how: SCOPE (e) (l.122-128) states the reading, gives the evidence (l.902-905: one turn of l(p) is delta^2, read correctly), and gives the uniqueness argument (four or two Gamma_p-fixed rays). That argument holds for any homomorphism Gamma_p -> PSL(2,R). At a light-like p the unipotent tangent action moves both arcs the same way, which a hyperbolic element of RP1 does not. It is marked 'not formalized'. L.17-19 and Main declarations l.74 now say 'under the double-cover reading' and 'read (SCOPE (e))'.

audit1_resolution.finding: AUDIT-1 minor: the HasLiftedHolonomy docstring overstated lt_apply
audit1_resolution.how: New lemma GX.lt_apply_of_strictMono (l.1483-1485): from (hD : StrictMono D) and (hDf : ∀ s, D (s + 1) = f (D s)), it gives D s < f (D s) for every s. This is eq> on the whole image for the witnesses of HasLiftedHolonomy. The proof `rw [← hDf]; exact hD (lt_add_one s)` is correct. The lemma is sorry-free and on the standard axioms. The docstring (l.1433-1435) now cites the lemma for 'every point x = D s' and says lt_apply 'extracts one such point', which is accurate for its ∃ x, x < f x. The REPORT dispatch_scope[2] lists the lemma and its note was updated.

audit1_resolution.finding: AUDIT-1 minor: the angle question lacked surgery-key and the visual structure
audit1_resolution.how: REPORT questions[0] and SCOPE (c) l.104-109 add (a), angle(delta) = 2 pi through Lemma surgery-key, and (b), the degree-one visual structure at time-like p only. They offer the author three options: uniform double cover, visual structure at time-like p, or renormalising delta = pi. The substance is correct. The line citation for P_theta is not: see findings[0].

findings.what: Wrong line citation. SCOPE (c) says 'with 𝒫_θ at l.2791–2807', and the REPORT says 'P_theta, the model of a particle of cone angle theta (l.2791-2807)'. 𝒫_θ does not occur in l.2791-2807. Those lines are the explicit example M(S) (\subsection{An explicit example}, l.2789, and Lemma bbslem:spacetime_particle_corresponding_singular, l.2802-2807), a surface with one cone point of angle θ. 𝒫_θ first appears in that lemma's proof, at l.2823 and l.2827: '𝒫_θ is the singular model space defined in Subsection sub:desgeom'. That model is the massive particle of cone angle θ, l.1142-1159 (sub:massiveparticle). The mathematics is right: 𝒫_θ is the particle of cone angle θ, so the regular case θ = 2π gives angle(δ) = 2π. The citation originated in AUDIT-1's own wording (angle_normalisation_check and finding 4), and the closer copied it. It would reach the author as a question.
findings.fix: Text only. In SCOPE (c) and REPORT questions[0], replace 'l.2791–2807' with 'l.2827, the massive particle of cone angle θ of l.1142–1159'. If wanted, add 'cf. the explicit example, l.2789–2807'. The master can apply this at graduation.
